request: In the WPS Register (WPS No, Process, PQR Ref, Review Date, Remark) write Check in Remark for every WPS whose PQR Ref does not start with PQR- (a blank PQR Ref counts too), and clear the Remark on the others. Tell me how many I marked.

On the Dispatch sheet (Dispatch No, Customer, Planned Date, Actual Date) highlight the whole row green when there is an Actual Date, and red when there is none and the Planned Date is before today. Rows that are neither stay without colour. Clear old highlights first so it can be run again, and tell me how many rows are red.

In the ITP Tracker (ITP No, Point, Inspection Status, Planned Date) write Overdue in a Flag column for every point that is not Closed and has a Planned Date before today, and clear the Flag on all the other points. Add the Flag heading if it isn't there. Tell me how many points are overdue.

In the Weld Log (Weld Seam No, Welder ID, Weld Date, Process, Visual, Remark) write Repeat in Remark for every row whose Weld Seam No appears more than once, and clear the Remark on the others. Seam numbers can have stray spaces or different upper and lower case, so 'ws-12' and ' WS-12 ' are the same seam. Tell me how many rows I marked.

From the Welder Quals sheet (Welder ID, Name, Process, Expiry Date) build a Qual Summary sheet with one row per process and three counts: how many qualifications are valid for more than 60 days, how many expire within the next 60 days, and how many have already expired. Processes in alphabetical order. Rows with no process or no valid Expiry Date are ignored.

From the WPS Register (WPS No, Process, PQR Ref, Review Date) write a Process Summary sheet with each process, how many WPS it has and how many of those have no PQR Ref, processes A to Z. Ignore rows with no process.

From the Material Certs sheet (Heat No, MTC No, Supplier) make a Supplier Summary sheet with the number of certificates per supplier and, next to it, how many of them have no MTC No, the supplier with the most certificates first. Ignore rows with no supplier.

Check the Dispatch sheet (Dispatch No, Job ID, Actual Date) against the Job Tracker (Job ID, Customer, Status). In the Job Tracker write Dispatched in a Dispatch Remark column for every job that has at least one dispatch with an Actual Date, and clear it on the others. Add the heading if it's missing. Job IDs sometimes have stray spaces. Tell me how many jobs are dispatched.

Compare the Welder Quals sheet (Welder ID, Process, Expiry Date) with the WPS Register (WPS No, Process). On a No WPS sheet, with the same headings as Welder Quals, list every qualification whose Process has no WPS in the register. Upper and lower case don't matter, so 'gtaw' and 'GTAW' match. Tell me how many I listed.

The Inspection Status cells in the ITP Tracker are messy: 'open', 'OPEN ', ' closed'. Make every status that is Open or Closed (ignoring case and stray spaces) read exactly Open or Closed, leave any other status alone, and tell me how many cells I changed.

On the Dispatch sheet (Dispatch No, Planned Date, Actual Date) some dates were typed as text like 2026-03-05. Turn those text dates in Planned Date and Actual Date into real dates, leave real dates and blank cells alone, and tell me how many cells I converted.

List on a Rejected Welds sheet every row of the NDE Report (Weld Seam No, Method, Result, Report Date) whose Result is Reject, with the same headings, newest Report Date first. The sheet is rebuilt every time it runs.

On a Short Receipts sheet list every line of the GRN sheet (GRN No, Part No, Ordered Qty, Received Qty) where Received Qty is less than Ordered Qty, with the same headings plus a Shortfall column (ordered minus received), biggest shortfall first. Lines with a blank or non-numeric quantity are skipped. The sheet is rebuilt every run.

For every row of the NDE Report sheet (Weld Seam No, Report File, Status) copy the file named in Report File from the Reports folder into the Archive folder (two folder paths I give the macro), and write Copied, Already there, Missing or Bad name in Status. Never overwrite or delete a file.

Count the rows on the Dispatch sheet (Dispatch No, Customer, Planned Date, Actual Date) that have no Actual Date and write that number as text in a new file called open_dispatches.txt in the Dispatch Docs folder (a folder path I give the macro). If the file already holds that number, leave it as it is. Write what happened in cell G1 of the sheet.

In the Dispatch sheet (Dispatch No, Planned Date, Actual Date, Days Late) put a formula in the Days Late column for every data row: Actual Date minus Planned Date, or blank when there is no Actual Date. Excel 2016 only.

On the NDE Report (Weld Seam No, Method, Result) hide every row except the Reject ones so only the rejected welds show, and tell me how many rows are visible below the headings. Running it again must give the same.

List every supplier from the Material Certs sheet (Heat No, MTC No, Supplier) once on a Suppliers sheet, with a Supplier heading, in alphabetical order. 'Acme Steel' and 'ACME STEEL' are the same supplier, and rows with no supplier are ignored. The sheet is rebuilt every run.

A welding procedure check tool, started with one macro. (1) In the WPS Register (WPS No, Process, PQR Ref, Review Date, Remark) write Check in Remark for every WPS whose PQR Ref is blank or whose Review Date is more than 365 days before today, and clear Remark on the others. (2) On a No WPS sheet list every qualification in Welder Quals (Welder ID, Process, Expiry Date) whose Process has no WPS in the register (upper and lower case don't matter). (3) On a Process Summary sheet write each process in the register with its number of WPS, how many are Check, and how many qualifications there are for it, processes A to Z. (4) On a WPS Summary sheet write the total WPS, the number of Check WPS and the number of qualifications with no WPS, with labels. The output sheets are rebuilt every run.

An inspection follow-up tool, started with one macro. (1) On a Rejects sheet list every row of the NDE Report (Weld Seam No, Method, Result, Report Date) whose Result is Reject, newest first, with the same headings. (2) In the ITP Tracker (ITP No, Point, Inspection Status, Planned Date) write Overdue in a Flag column for every point that is not Closed and is planned before today, and clear it on the others. (3) On a Method Summary sheet write, for each NDE method, how many results are Accept, Repair and Reject, methods A to Z. (4) On an Inspection Summary sheet write the number of rejects, overdue points and methods, with labels. The output sheets are rebuilt every run.
